text:
Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Participate(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenshipUS(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenshipTaiwan(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
Official(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
ManagerAtGazprom(x) ::: x is a manager at Gazprom.
HoldTaiwaneseCitizenship(x) ::: x holds Taiwanese citizenship.
Vladimir ::: Vladimir.
Ekaterina ::: Ekaterina.
Premises:
∀x (CitizenshipUS(x) → CanRegister(x)) ::: Everyone with US citizenship can register to vote.
∀x (CitizenshipUS(x) ∨ CitizenshipTaiwan(x)) ::: Everyone has either US or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬∃x (Official(x) ∧ HoldTaiwaneseCitizenship(x)) ::: No Russian Federation official holds Taiwanese citizenship.
¬(HoldTaiwaneseCitizenship(Vladimir) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(Vladimir)) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
CanRegister(Ekaterina) ∨ Official(Ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote or is an official.
Conclusion:
Official(Vladimir) ::: Vladimir is a Russian Federation official.
